title: Brown founds NICAP; Hillenkoetter on board

tellings.quote: When Brown returned from the International Geophysical Year, he created NICAP, or the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena.
realize that he started NICAP, which was the first civilian UFO tracking program in 1956.
tellings.difference: Calls it the first civilian UFO tracking program and does not mention Hillenkoetter or the International Geophysical Year.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Townsend Brown founding NICAP, the civilian UFO group, in 1956.

plain: A scientist named Thomas Townsend Brown is said to have founded NICAP, the National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena, in 1956, a group Michels calls the first civilian UFO tracking programme. Michels tells it himself in two episodes: in one he says Brown created it after returning from the International Geophysical Year, a worldwide science effort, and names a man called Roscoe Hillenkoetter in connection with it. In the other he simply calls it the first civilian UFO tracker and leaves out Hillenkoetter and the science year. It matters to Michels because it would put a government-linked scientist at the start of public UFO research.
